subject: FEC681A8D62B4EA3B73B57371D4A34C7
introduction: “Let your eye be chaste, your hand faithful, your tongue truthful and your heart enlightened.” The guide’s first sentence sets chastity among the virtues of a whole character and addresses it to everyone. What follows includes a striking early remark that a charge of unchastity falls on men as on women, the insistence that modesty must not keep girls from education, the description of marriage as a fortress, and plain rules of conduct. The Sermon on the Mount, Job and the Qur’an all begin, like the first reading, with the eye, and the Qur’an addresses the men first. Joseph in Potiphar’s house is scripture’s model. The critics matter here. Wollstonecraft saw women’s whole worth reduced to “a single virtue”; Blake saw priests binding desire with briars; Whitman would call nothing in the body unclean; Milton would not praise a virtue that has never met its adversary. And twice the Gospel of John is brought in for the forbearance on which the guide ends.
questions: The first reading speaks of eye, hand, tongue and heart together. What is lost when chastity is taken out of that company and made a subject by itself?
Wollstonecraft objected that women were judged by “a single virtue”. Which readings in the guide resist that reduction, and which might seem to invite it?
Milton will not praise “a fugitive and cloistered virtue”; reading 13 will not let chastity prevent education. How should purity and exposure to the world be combined?
Blake’s priests bound “with briars my joys and desires”. What distinguishes self-command from repression, in the readings and in experience?
“He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone”; “go, and sin no more.” How does the guide hold a demanding standard together with forbearance toward those who fall short?

outside.why: “Let your eye be chaste.” The Sermon on the Mount moves the commandment from the act to the eye: whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
Job’s defence of his life begins there: I made a covenant with mine eyes.
The Qur’an addresses the men first: tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them.
The reading turns a charge of unchastity made against women back on those who make it. He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
Strength is not a matter of physique or sex: behind the veil of chastity may stand the stronger person. Wollstonecraft of women: I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.
The Bible’s pattern of chastity under pressure is a man, Joseph in Potiphar’s house: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

All are summoned to chastity, trustworthiness and religiosity. This is the will of God, even your sanctification: that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour.
Chastity is called the first ornament. Peter: not the outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold; but the hidden man of the heart.

Wollstonecraft protested that for women attention is confined to a single virtue, chastity, as if a woman’s honour were safe once that was, whatever else she neglected. Readings 8 and 17 to 20 praise chastity as women’s greatest ornament. How does the guide’s first reading, addressed to all, answer her?
Marriage is a fortress that preserves chastity. Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled.
Rules of conduct between unmarried men and women. Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace.

Blake went to the Garden of Love and saw priests in black gowns walking their rounds, and binding with briars my joys and desires. He speaks for everyone who has experienced such rules as that. What must a teaching on chastity do so as not to be what he saw?
Girls are to be trained in knowledge and in character. Train up a child in the way he should go.
Chastity is necessary, “but not to the degree that it prevents education and learning”. Strengthen the female mind by enlarging it, and there will be an end to blind obedience.
Milton on virtue kept safe by being kept ignorant: I cannot praise a fugitive and cloistered virtue, unexercised and unbreathed, that never sallies out and sees her adversary.
Manifest “the purity of the highest realm”. Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
Chaste and faithful women who suffer injustice and slander. Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.
“Grieve not at what hath befallen thee, but hold fast unto purity.” Hamlet to Ophelia, bitterly: be thou as chaste as ice, as pure as snow, thou shalt not escape calumny.
“All pure things are acceptable.” Whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report, think on these things.

Paul to Titus: unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure. Purity on this saying is first a quality of the one who sees. How does that qualify rules about what may be seen?
“Clean bodies, pure hearts.” Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost?
One who shows wickedness and lust “is not … of the True One”. Ye shall know them by their fruits.

The people of Bahá must show the greatest chastity. Iago, of all people, states the principle of self-command: our bodies are our gardens, to the which our wills are gardeners; we have reason to cool our raging motions.

Marriage protects from “immoral deeds”. Whitman declared himself the poet of the body as well as the soul, and would not call any part of it unclean. What in the readings’ praise of marriage agrees with him, and where do they part?
A chaste and holy life as the controlling principle in every relation. Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.

Youth are to avoid what arouses passion. The guide’s arc ends in “personal forbearance”. To the woman taken in adultery: neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more. How do a high standard for oneself and forbearance toward others live together?

shortfall: Several readings repeat one sentence of counsel to women correspondents (hold fast to chastity; it is your greatest adornment); they share companions.

matthew-looketh-on-a-woman.text: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart

job-covenant-with-mine-eyes.text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid

hebrews-marriage-is-honourable.text: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled

timothy-flee-youthful-lusts.text: Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart

thessalonians-possess-his-vessel.text: For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication: That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour

quran-lower-their-gaze.text: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do.
